title: What a booking website costs for a studio
summary: The public price list has no line called booking website. Here are the published from figures for a ready site, a premium site and Local Desk, and what to settle before a quote.
metaDescription: The public price list has no line called booking website. Here are the published from figures for a ready site, a premium site and Local Desk, and what to settle before a quote.
author: OMNI101 Studio

sections.h2: What a studio means by a booking website
paragraphs: OMNI101 Studio, 24 October 2026. For many studios, booking is not a full calendar engine. It is a page that explains the work, shows how a meeting happens, and offers a way to ask for a time. Sometimes a form is enough: name, contact, kind of request, a time window. Sometimes it is a calendar tied to the person who receives people, with duration, notice and cancellation. The price changes because the work changes, not because the word booking has a fixed fee.

Before you read a number, write what should happen after the click. Does the request only land in email, or does it enter a list someone confirms? Does the person see a held time, or a note that the studio will reply? Who can move the appointment, and how late? If those answers are missing, any figure is a starting point, not a closed quote.

sections.h2: The from figures on the public list
paragraphs: On the studio's public price list, generated on 24 October 2026, there is no line named booking website. The numbers below are from thresholds, not the price of a measured project. Ready site: setup from €1,600 and a monthly fee from €39. Premium site: setup from €4,400 and a monthly fee from €69. Each line has three levels, Essential, Recommended and Complete. The from figure is the published entry level, not the detail of a diary.

For a studio that wants a local page together with a responder, there is the Local Desk bundle, Essential level. The list states it in dollars, not euros: from 1,900 USD once and from 148 USD a month. The products named in the bundle are the ready site and the responder. The responder alone has a monthly fee from €99 and a one-off of zero: no setup from above zero is published. None of these lines says a connected calendar is already included.

sections.h2: How to read setup and monthly fee together
paragraphs: Setup is the work to put the first version online: page structure, texts placed, form, checks. The monthly fee is what stays on after that, including hosting and the time to keep the page usable. Looking only at setup makes an ongoing cost look small. Adding a year of fees without knowing what they cover makes the opposite mistake. For the ready site the published minimum reading is setup from €1,600 plus a monthly fee from €39. For the premium site, setup from €4,400 plus a monthly fee from €69. Those are floors, not a real studio's total.

Do not convert the Local Desk bundle into euros in this article: the list publishes it in USD. Placing it next to the ready site in euros, with no exchange rate in the list, mixes two currencies. If the studio works in euros, the quote question is which line describes the work: the euro line or the dollar bundle. The answer is the scope, not a rate invented here.

sections.h2: What those figures do not include
paragraphs: A from threshold does not by itself include several people on one diary, a deposit, message reminders, or moving a diary that is already full. It does not include copy written instead of the studio if the studio does not supply it, or new photographs. It does not include a promise that the site will bring appointments. A page can make the request clear. It cannot decide how many people will use it.

Even a short form has an edge. You need to say where name and contact go, how long they stay, and who can read them. An email and a store with access rules are two different jobs. If booking touches health data or children's data, write that scope before the price, not in a note after signature. The price list does not replace that sentence.

sections.h2: What to prepare before you ask for the number
paragraphs: A few concrete lines are enough. Who receives the person. How long a meeting usually is. How much notice is needed to ask for a time, and until when it can be cancelled. Whether a deposit is required and, if so, which tool the studio already uses to take it. Which details the client must write and which they must not. A sample week stops you designing a calendar that does not match the real day.

With that list you can see whether the ready site is enough, whether the premium site is the line to open, or whether Local Desk is the row to read. Without the list, from is a label. The next step is the linked offer: the published figure sits next to what is included and what is quoted apart. This article does not close the quote.

faq.a: No. It is the ready site's setup from figure on the public list. Booking has no row of its own. A calendar, reminders or a deposit, if you need them, are described and quoted. They are not deduced from that figure.

faq.q: Why is Local Desk in dollars?
faq.a: Because the public list records it that way: currency USD, from 1,900 once and from 148 a month, Essential level, products ready site and responder. This article does not calculate a euro exchange.

faq.q: Can the monthly fee be removed?
faq.a: The list publishes those lines with a monthly from fee. Turning off hosting and updates is a scope choice, not a zero row already written. It belongs in the quote.

title: Replying to Google reviews without wasting time
summary: A draft reply to Google reviews removes the blank page. Publishing stays with a person at the studio, through an approval step you can see.
metaDescription: A draft reply to Google reviews removes the blank page. Publishing stays with a person at the studio, through an approval step you can see.
author: OMNI101 Studio

paragraphs: OMNI101 Studio, 24 October 2026. A new review arrives while the studio is in the room or on a job. A good reply needs two things that are missing in that moment: a few minutes and the right sentence. The usual result is a queue. Not because the review does not matter, but because nobody has a fixed place where the reply is already half written.

The time is lost on the blank page, not on the publish click. The person who must reply rereads the review, picks the tone, avoids arguing in public, and does not promise what the studio cannot keep. If every review starts from zero, even three notes a week become work that slips to the Monday after.

sections.h2: A draft is not a published reply
paragraphs: A tool can read the review text and propose a draft in the studio's tone: thanks, the fact mentioned, an invitation to continue in private if there is a problem. The draft is text. It is not the reply visible on the listing. Until a person at the studio approves it, it does not go out.

Keep that distinction in the flow, not in a slogan. The step is called approval: the draft sits on a list, with a source for the proposed text and a name for the person who says yes. If nobody says yes, the review stays without a public reply. That outcome is acceptable. It is better than text that left on its own.

sections.h2: Where the person who approves sits
paragraphs: You need a role, not a vague turn. One person, or a substitute when they are away, looks at the queue at a stated time: end of morning, on days you are open, for example. They do not have to write from zero. They read the review, read the draft, fix a sentence if it is wrong, and publish, or discard.

Approval is where the studio stays responsible for what appears under its name. A draft can miss a detail, mix up a service, or sound softer or harder than usual. The person who approves knows the client and the fact. The tool does not, even when the text looks tidy.

If the queue grows past what that person can read, the fix is not to remove approval. Shorten the draft, narrow which cases enter the queue, or move the time. Removing the human yes to empty the list moves the risk onto the public listing.

Do not publish on its own a refund, an apology about a disputed fact, a health detail, another person's name, or a reply to a review the studio does not recognise. Those cases leave the normal draft and go to a person, with the original text beside them. The tool can flag them. It does not close them.

Do not invent a star policy, an average reply time, or an effect on bookings. This article does not have those figures. The work described here is only this: less blank page, a human yes before publishing, a queue you can see.

A useful rhythm is small and repeatable. New reviews enter a list. A draft appears under each one. The person who approves clears what they can read in that pass and leaves the rest visible, not hidden. At the end of the week you only look at whether one person can still read the queue. If they cannot, you change the scope. You do not declare a result.

The link to the offer is the assistant that prepares the draft inside the studio's flow. The price of that work is not in this article: it is on the offer, with its from figures. The point here is the boundary. The tool proposes. A person at the studio publishes.

faq.q: Does the reply post itself on the Google listing?
faq.a: No. The draft stays in the queue until a person at the studio approves it. Without that yes, there is no public reply.
A named person at the studio, with a substitute if they are away. The role is to read, correct if needed, publish or discard. It is not an anonymous step.

faq.q: Can every review be answered the same way?
faq.a: No. Refunds, disputed facts, sensitive data and reviews you do not recognise leave the normal draft and stay with a person, original text beside them.

title: Automating quotes and follow-up in a small business
summary: A quote gets lost between the first message and the nudge. You can automate the trail and the draft. Sending the price, and closing, stay with a person.
metaDescription: A quote gets lost between the first message and the nudge. You can automate the trail and the draft. Sending the price, and closing, stay with a person.
author: OMNI101 Studio

paragraphs: OMNI101 Studio, 24 October 2026. In a small business a quote does not vanish inside a large system. It vanishes between email, a sheet and the memory of whoever spoke to the client. The first message arrives. Someone answers by voice. The number is never written down. Two weeks later nobody knows whether a nudge went out.

Follow-up has the same hole. A generic reminder, the same for everyone, does not say where that request stood. No reminder leaves the client in silence. The useful work is not sending more messages. It is knowing, for each request, what the last step was, what the next step is, and who must do it.

sections.h2: What can start on its own
paragraphs: What can start on its own is what does not commit a price and does not speak to the client in the business's name. Log the request on a list. Mark the date. Attach the original message. Prepare a draft of answers to questions you already know: what is included, what is missing, which details are still needed. Tell the internal person that a draft is waiting.

An internal reminder can also start on a stated date: in three days, if nobody has marked an outcome, the row returns to the top. The reminder speaks to someone inside the business, not to the client. The trail then does not depend on memory, and the client does not receive text nobody has read.

The price, the discount, the delivery date you promise, and the yes that turns a draft into a quote you send, stay with a person. They are commitments. Well-shaped text does not make them true. The person reads the draft, changes the lines that are wrong, and only then sends, or decides not to send.

The same holds for follow-up toward the client. A nudge can be prepared. It leaves when the person following that request confirms that the tone and the moment are right. If the client already said no, or asked not to be contacted, the row closes. You do not press on with an automation that did not read that sentence.

sections.h2: What you need before you connect the sheets
paragraphs: You need three short lists, written by the business, not invented by the tool. The states of a request: just arrived, in draft, sent, accepted, refused, to call back. The minimum details required to make a price: quantity, place, timing, constraints. The cases you do not automate: urgencies, disputes, amounts above a threshold the business chooses.

Without those lists, connecting email to a sheet moves the mess. It does not shrink it. With the lists, the flow has a start, visible steps and an outcome. If a step fails, the row stays in the queue with a readable error. It does not disappear. Someone knows they must step in.

sections.h2: A scope that fits a small business
paragraphs: The right scope fits the week of the people who already write quotes. It does not ask for a new department. It asks that every request have a row, that the draft wait for a yes, and that the internal nudge fire only if the row is still open. At month end you look at whether rows without an outcome are fewer than on the previous sheet. If you did not keep the previous sheet, you do not declare an improvement: you start counting from that month.

The linked offer is automation of one repetitive process. The from figures for that work sit on the offer, not here. This article does not promise more contracts. It describes a place where the quote and the follow-up do not depend on the memory of a single day.

faq.a: No. The tool can log the request and prepare a draft. Price, discount, promised timing and sending stay with a person in the business.

faq.q: Does the nudge write to the client without a yes?
faq.a: Not in the scope described here. The automatic reminder is internal. The message to the client leaves only if the person following the request confirms it, and it does not leave if the client asked not to be contacted.

faq.q: Where do you start if everything is in email today?
faq.a: With the states of a request, the minimum details needed to make a price, and the cases that stay manual. Without those three lists, connecting tools does not tidy the work.

title: What to ask an AI agency before you sign
summary: Before you sign with an AI agency, ask for the concrete job, who approves, which data leaves, and what the price does not include. A tidy demo is not enough.
metaDescription: Before you sign with an AI agency, ask for the concrete job, who approves, which data leaves, and what the price does not include. A tidy demo is not enough.
author: OMNI101 Studio

sections.h2: Before the contract, the actual job
paragraphs: OMNI101 Studio, 24 October 2026. An agency that talks about artificial intelligence can show a smooth demo and leave a vague assignment in the contract. Before you sign, ask which job in your process changes next week. Not the sector in the abstract. The step: a reply draft, a quote row, a page, a list. If the step cannot be named, there is no assignment yet.

Also ask what stays the same. A tool that proposes text does not replace the person who knows the client, the price and the constraint. If the agency describes only what switches on, and not what a person must still do, the scope is incomplete. The contract should name both.

Ask which data enter the tool and which must not. Client messages, price lists, names, internal files: for each, where they are read, whether they leave the studio, how long they stay. Ask for a list, not an adjective. Secure does not say whether a document stays in your space or is sent elsewhere.

Ask who may accept a result. If a reply can leave, a price can be sent, or a page can go online with no responsible name, the flow has no edge. The name can be yours or someone you name. It has to exist before signature, not after the first mistake.

Ask what happens when the result is wrong. A correction, a new draft, a stop. An assignment without that step forces you to discover it in production. Also ask whether you can take texts, configuration and access with you if you end the relationship, and in what format.

sections.h2: Price, time and what is not included
paragraphs: Ask for the figure in two parts, if both exist: what you pay to stand the first flow up, and what you pay to keep it on. Ask what that figure does not include: extra connections, copy written instead of you, training for more people, urgencies, volume past a threshold. One figure with no exclusions is not a quote. It is a title.

Ask for the date of the first usable version and who must be present to approve it. A schedule that depends on your materials should say so, with the list of materials. If the agency does not separate its time from the time it waits for you, the slip becomes an argument. Better to write it first.

Ask how a proof is read. A demo on sample data shows the mechanism. It does not show your price list, your tone, your awkward cases. Ask for a proof on your material, even a small one, before a long commitment. If that is not possible, ask why, and what you risk by signing without having seen it.

sections.h2: How to recognise a useful answer
paragraphs: A useful answer is specific. It names the step, the human yes, the data that do not enter, the starting price and the cost that stays, the exclusions, the date of the first version. A useless answer talks about transformation, about results not measured in your work, or about tools by name instead of the flow. If you hear a product name and you do not hear who presses send, ask again.

Do not sign on the sentence that the agency will use a famous model. The model changes. Your need does not: a described task, a boundary on data, a person who approves, a way to stop. This article does not score agencies and does not report how many businesses have signed. It lists the questions. You read the answers on your own case.

If you want to see how OMNI101 Studio places an assistant inside a flow, with a draft and a check, the linked offer is the assistant offer. The terms and the from figures are there, not in this guide.

faq.a: No. A demo on sample data shows the mechanism. Before you sign, ask for the step in your process, a proof on your material if that is possible, and what the price does not include.
The concrete task, which data do not enter, the name of whoever approves a send or a publication, the starting price and what stays on, the exclusions, and how a wrong result is corrected.
No. It does not assign scores and it does not report market numbers. It prepares the questions. Read the answers on the contract in front of you.

If you want to see how OMNI101 Studio places an assistant inside a flow, with a draft and a check, the linked offer is the assistant offer. The terms and the from figures are there, not in this guide.

Is a demo enough to sign? No. A demo on sample data shows the mechanism. Before you sign, ask for the step in your process, a proof on your material if that is possible, and what the price does not include.

What must the scope contain? The concrete task, which data do not enter, the name of whoever approves a send or a publication, the starting price and what stays on, the exclusions, and how a wrong result is corrected.
Does this article compare agencies? No. It does not assign scores and it does not report market numbers. It prepares the questions. Read the answers on the contract in front of you.
